scientific_hypothesis: A periodic quarter-wave stack using ThSi2 (high-index) and YbF3 (low-index) on CaF2 substrate will achieve dual-band transmission at 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm through constructive interference, while providing stopband rejection at 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm through destructive interference, with 16 layers sufficient to reach >70% peak transmittance in passbands.
expected_advantages: High index contrast reduces required layer count
16 layers leaves margin for future complexity
Log-normal seeding avoids local minima from deterministic quarter-wave start
known_risks: Material registry may not have ThSi2 or YbF3 optical constants
Quarter-wave stack produces single broad passband, may not separate CO/CO2 bands cleanly
16 layers may be insufficient for deep stopband rejection
expected_observations: best_target_score should rise more slowly than Route 1 due to lower index contrast requiring more precise thickness control
tightest_margin may be lower than Route 1 if stopband depth is insufficient with 12 pairs
valid_candidates should remain high as Si3N4/MgF2 are low-loss dielectrics
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if tightest_margin remains below 0.1 for four consecutive rounds, reduce pair count to 11 and add matching layers at substrate interface
